name: FHFA Page on Final Rule for Automated Valuation Model Quality Control
title: FHFA Page on Final Rule for Automated Valuation Model Quality Control
answer: This is the FHFA page for the interagency final rule implementing Dodd-Frank quality control standards for automated valuation models used by mortgage originators and secondary market issuers to value collateral for loans secured by a consumer's principal dwelling. Its most useful point is that covered institutions making certain credit or securitization decisions must adopt policies, practices, procedures, and control systems for AVMs, including standards meant to ensure confidence in estimates, protect against data manipulation, and avoid conflicts of interest.

sections.body: The Federal Housing Finance Agency publishes this page about a final rule adopted by six agencies: the OCC, Board, FDIC, NCUA, CFPB, and FHFA. It is a regulatory summary, not the full rule text in the supplied material. Its scope is the use of automated valuation models by mortgage originators and secondary market issuers when determining the collateral worth of a mortgage secured by a consumer's principal dwelling. The supplied text does not state a publication date. It includes contact details for FHFA staff and repeats the summary.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page states that the agencies are adopting a final rule to implement quality control standards mandated by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act for the use of automated valuation models by mortgage originators and secondary market issuers in determining the collateral worth of a mortgage secured by a consumer's principal dwelling. Under the final rule, institutions that engage in certain credit decisions or securitization determinations must adopt policies, practices, procedures, and control systems to ensure that AVMs used in these transactions to determine the value of mortgage collateral adhere to quality control standards. Those standards are designed to ensure a high level of confidence in the estimates produced by AVMs, protect against the manipulation of data, and seek to avoid conflicts of interest. The supplied text ends there, so it does not list the remaining standards or the full compliance details. The page also provides FHFA contacts for further information, Julie Giesbrecht and Karen Heidel, with phone numbers and email addresses, and notes TTY/TRS access through 711. The summary appears twice in the harvested text, which suggests the page is a short landing or summary page rather than the complete final rule.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source names six agencies: OCC, Board, FDIC, NCUA, CFPB, and FHFA. It gives FHFA contact numbers for Julie Giesbrecht at (202) 557-9866 and Karen Heidel at (202) 738-7753, and says TTY/TRS users can dial 711. It states the rule implements Dodd-Frank quality control standards for AVMs used by mortgage originators and secondary market issuers in determining collateral worth for a mortgage secured by a consumer's principal dwelling. It lists three aims for the standards: high confidence in AVM estimates, protection against data manipulation, and avoiding conflicts of interest. It gives no numerical thresholds, compliance dates, or model accuracy figures.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in real estate would use this source because it marks a federal regulatory baseline for AVMs, which are a core AI application in mortgage collateral valuation. The page shows that the rule applies to mortgage originators and secondary market issuers making certain credit or securitization determinations, so it is relevant to how AI valuation models are governed in lending and securitization. It also signals the compliance themes regulators attach to these models: confidence in estimates, data manipulation risk, and conflicts of interest. The supplied text does not go into implementation detail, but it identifies the agencies and the rule's intended scope.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Real Estate

sections.body: The supplied text is a short, repeated summary rather than the full final rule. It does not state a publication date, effective date, compliance deadlines, covered thresholds, or the complete list of quality control standards. It does not explain how AVMs are built, tested, or audited, and it does not address real estate uses outside mortgage collateral decisions. The page is official and non commercial, but it is partial and truncated, so it should be treated as a pointer to the rule rather than a full account of it.
